reference_summary: The first fan bank's start threshold in the temperature controller was retained at 92°C rather than 78°C. The cooling control logic used an ambient bias that remained at zero when the outdoor temperature exceeded 43°C. Although ambient temperature was 47°C, this value alone was not the root cause; the transformer load was only 75 percent of rating. A 40 MVA auxiliary transformer was taken out of service, raising the station load demand on the target transformer. The manual selector blocked this remote command; the pump did not energise. The leaked current shifted the reported top-oil temperature downward by 6°C continuously. At 15:04, the winding hot-spot relay operated and sent a trip signal to the transformer circuit breaker. The Synthetic Grid network lost 116 MW of firm supply when the 220 kV ring separated. After the trip, two technicians manually closed the cooling valve and turned both pump switches to forced-run. The control algorithms were replaced with the archived 2019 revision, resetting the start setpoint to 78°C.

reference_summary: The cooling controller's integrator error was negative; valve reference fell while temperature rose. The outdoor air sensor was mounted in a still pocket, far from the natural draft. The day was hot, yet the 48.5°C peak was not the primary cause of the shutdown; load had been within 98% of planned limits. A 55 kVA motor-driven pump started, reducing the oil level in the sump and triggering the low-level switch. The inlet valve remained at its minimum stop, overruled by the negative integrator. The fan speed reduction forced the top-oil temperature to increase at a rate of 1.4 K per minute. The transformer relay detached the incoming feeder at 17:13 and isolated the faulty bay. The synthetic local load received a 35% voltage drop for 1.8 seconds before the capacitor banks switched out. The operator manually opened the inlet valve using a 500 mm wrench after local confirmation. Portable fans were directed at the radiator intake until the oil trend reached 70°C.
